acceptance: A tuning file can set the distribution column per table and mark tables as reference tables; the CLI flag still works and its precedence over the file is documented
Every tuning request is recorded in the ledger as applied_verified, not applied, or failed, with a reason, and is verified against the Citus catalog (pg_dist_partition)
Live run of TPC-H SF0.01 on a Citus amd64 environment, with the catalog evidence recorded in the PR
Platform docs page describes the tuning method and its limits
context: Owner request 2026-10-17: "There should be a method for tuning these platforms." Local live verification wasn't possible because Citus has no arm64 image. Verify on an amd64 runner (CI or a nightly cell) or with an emulated amd64 container.
description: PostgreSQL tuning now partitions tables and runs CLUSTER (#3098, #3092), but Citus skips both (benchbox/platforms/citus.py:34, execution_partitioning_supported = False). Citus's only layout control is `--citus-distribution-column` (citus.py:85-117), which distributes every table on one column and ignores the tuning file. Add a tuning-file method: per-table distribution columns (create_distributed_table), reference tables for small dimensions, an optional columnar access method, and native PostgreSQL partitioning where Citus allows it. Record each request in the applied-tuning ledger as applied_verified, not applied, or failed, with reasons.
